column1: # The curated list behind the parts catalog. `tools/build-catalog.mjs` reads this, fetches
# the bases and writes crates/seqcore/data/parts.tsv. This file is the curation; the
# generated one is derived and should never be edited by hand.
#   id        stable slug, also the catalog's key
#   name      what the app shows, and what src/lib/labinfo.ts matches on: see
#   molecule  `dna`, or `protein` for an entry searched in all six frames. A tag's DNA
#             varies with the codons someone chose, so a peptide entry is the reliable way
#             to find one; the DNA rows cover the common choices too.
#   from      where the bases come from:
#               ncbi:ACC:gene=NAME     the record's own CDS (or gene) with that /gene
#               ncbi:ACC:TYPE@a..b     that feature, asserting the record still says a..b
#               amrfinder:SYMBOL       first allele of that gene symbol in AMR_CDS.fa
#               literal                the bases in this row
#               defined:ACC:a..b       a record's bases, but an extent we decided
#                                      ourselves because the record marks the feature as a
#                                      single base; `reference` must justify the extent
#   sequence  only for `literal` rows: the bases, or residues for a protein row
#   protein   expected translation; the generator fails if the bases don't give it, which
#             is how a typo in a hand-entered tag gets caught
#   reference `PMID n` or `DOI x`. Leave it empty where the source carries its own — an
#             `ncbi` row takes the record's primary reference, `uniprot` the entry's and
#             `fpbase` the protein's DOI, so those are right by construction. A `literal`
#             row has nothing to fetch, and a `defined` row needs the paper that justifies
#             the extent, so for those it is required and hand-curated.
#   citation  first author, year and journal of that `reference`, required whenever
#             `reference` is hand-curated. The generator looks the PMID or DOI up and
#             fails the build unless the author and year agree, which is what stops a
#             citation from drifting onto the wrong paper.
#   note      one line for the catalog and the review dialog
